implementation.owner: TeamRosterTransitions is a cohesive use case of the existing Team owner using the same authority fence/state, not a second Team/runtime owner. Finite read/replace/original lookup methods are available over the captured Host NDJSON envelope.

Descriptive role is preserved in product settings while controller projection uses canonical lead/member authority.
implementation.identity: Expected revision and current read/admin grants precede admission. Monotonic product roster version distinguishes a return to previous values. Existing names retain product IDs; restored removed names retain their product identity but never revive old grants or native targets. New members get a deterministic command-qualified ID. Cross-operation command reuse conflicts; opaque command IDs are not trimmed.
implementation.publication: Decision, membership/grant transitions and original receipt publish atomically in Team state. A captured config preimage/desired projection is recovered idempotently before subsequent policy. Foreign config bytes hold recovery instead of being overwritten. Replay returns original command/revision without rerunning membership policy.
implementation.runtime: Changes require synchronous proof of unopened or closed/released resources outside the Team lock, then current authority/revision is rechecked before publication. Async proof is rejected. Live/pending/unknown custody and unresolved Task/delivery obligations hold without a roster receipt. Confirmed edits detach prior delivery targets and revoke bound/removed agent grants; they never allocate or stop providers.
implementation.cold: A stale static runtime descriptor cannot silently apply old settings or allocate a replacement. Changed Teams are excluded from static native composition after restart; product reads/mutations remain usable while Launch configuration is explicitly unconfigured. Runtime/launch journals and product Task/inbox bytes are not deleted.
implementation.bounds: Private Team state1MiB,1024 roster receipts and1024 removed members. Exhaustion holds before publication without deleting outcomes. This slice does not add retention/GC or claim unbounded history capacity.
